sources.title: Non-Directional Liquidity Capture & Market Making Overview
sources.relevance: Synthesized knowledge overview identifying critical Kalshi adaptation unknowns (FIFO vs pro-rata matching, fee structure, position merging equivalent), six structural edges, and non-linear curve as primary differentiator

overview.description:
A fully non-directional market-making system for Kalshi binary event contracts (crypto price threshold contracts such as BTC/ETH above/below strike prices) that profits exclusively from liquidity provision, spread capture, and structural order-book mechanics. The system places simultaneous bid ladders on both YES and NO sides of a contract, captures the bid-ask spread on every matched trade, manages inventory through offsetting position settlement (capital recycling), and uses Stoikov-Avellaneda optimal quoting with Bayesian probability updates and Kelly criterion position sizing. The system never takes a directional bet — all profit derives from being the liquidity layer that other participants trade against.

Non-linear order curve distribution concentrates volume at high-fill-probability price levels, identified as the single most important differentiator among market-making bots (Curve Alchemist +$18,920 outperformed flat Ladder Larry +$12,450 by 52% and Merge Phantom +$9,830 by 92% in a 24-hour head-to-head under identical conditions).

Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated prediction market exchange legal for US residents, operating a central limit order book (CLOB) with YES/NO contracts priced 1-99 cents, cash-settled in USD. All Kalshi prices are in cents (not dollars). Kalshi's fee model charges on settlement (typically 1-7 cents per contract) rather than per-trade, which fundamentally changes spread calculation — the system must account for expected settlement cost amortized across the fill-to-settlement lifecycle. Kalshi's orderbook tends to be thinner than larger unregulated venues, which is advantageous for market making: wider natural spreads create more profit per fill.

Six non-predictive structural edges complement the core spread capture: base rate neglect, cross-market inconsistency, mechanical price moves in thin liquidity, cross-platform comparison, certainty overpaying, and time decay mispricing. These inform adaptive spread width and position sizing without requiring outcome prediction.

Critical Kalshi platform unknowns that must be resolved in Phase 0 before full implementation: (1) FIFO vs pro-rata matching engine — determines whether speed-based queue priority or capital-based sizing is the dominant competitive axis; (2) maker vs taker fee structure — whether maker rebates exist that subsidize liquidity provision; (3) position merging equivalent — whether YES+NO positions can be combined for early settlement or must be held to expiry; (4) API rate limits and WebSocket capabilities for HF order management.
objectives: Capture bid-ask spread on both YES and NO contracts simultaneously without directional exposure

Implement Stoikov-Avellaneda reservation price model: r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) for inventory-aware quote centering, with optimal spread delta = gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1 + gamma/kappa) where kappa is estimated market order arrival rate
Use Bayesian probability updates P(H|D) = P(D|H)*P(H)/P(D) anchored to external CEX reference prices to maintain internal fair-value estimate before market reprices

Deploy non-linear order curve distribution (power-law or adaptive curve) that allocates more volume to high-fill-probability price levels near current mid — the primary differentiator identified across all source material

Implement capital recycling engine that tracks opposing YES+NO holdings and determines optimal exit strategy (hold-to-settle vs early-exit via opposing limit orders), accounting for Kalshi's settlement fee structure

Integrate six non-predictive structural edges (base rate neglect, cross-market inconsistency, mechanical price moves, cross-platform comparison, certainty overpaying, time decay mispricing) as a meta-layer informing spread width and position sizing
Maintain market-neutral inventory at all times with hard inventory skew limits, using Stoikov reservation price adjustment to skew quotes away from accumulated exposure
Achieve consistent 2-5% monthly return on deployed capital through spread capture and structural imbalance accumulation, accounting for Kalshi's settlement fee structure (1-7 cents per contract)
Operate autonomously across multiple concurrent Kalshi crypto price threshold contract windows
Resolve critical Kalshi platform unknowns (matching engine rules, fee structure, position merging equivalent, API capabilities) in Phase 0 before committing to full implementation
constraints: Zero directional bets — the system must never take a net directional position intentionally. All profit derives from spread capture, structural imbalance, and capital recycling

All ladder orders must be placed as limit orders only. The spread calculation must factor in the expected settlement fee (1-7 cents per contract) — only deploy on contracts where expected captured spread exceeds expected settlement cost

Requires low-latency infrastructure: order placement must complete within 200ms for competitive queue priority (assuming FIFO matching — if Kalshi uses pro-rata, latency requirement relaxes but capital requirement increases). US-based cloud instance (AWS us-east-1) recommended
Must operate within Kalshi REST API rate limits and order submission constraints. Batch operations (up to 20 orders per call) are essential for efficient ladder management

Minimum $500 deployed capital for meaningful fill frequency; optimal at $5,000-$50,000 for full ladder deployment. Subject to Kalshi's per-market position limits (typically $25K-$100K notional per market)
Cannot backtest accurately — fills depend on real-time counterparty interaction and queue position. All validation must occur through live paper-mode on Kalshi's demo environment
Must handle sudden market reversals that load inventory heavily on the losing side — this is the primary source of realized losses for market makers
Kalshi requires full KYC (SSN, ID verification) — account must be set up and verified before development begins
Position limits vary per market on Kalshi — the system must query and respect per-market position limits dynamically
Non-linear curve optimization requires iterative live testing and cannot be solved analytically — start with power-law exponent 1.5 and calibrate from fill rate data
assumptions: Kalshi crypto price threshold contracts maintain sufficient liquidity for bid ladder deployment. Thinner books relative to unregulated venues are expected and beneficial — wider natural spreads improve market-making profitability
Bid-ask spreads remain wide enough (minimum 3-5 cents after accounting for expected settlement fees) to generate positive expected value
Kalshi operates a CLOB with FIFO queue priority at each price level (to be confirmed in Phase 0 — if pro-rata, the architecture shifts from speed optimization to capital optimization)
Structural imbalance effect persists: trending price naturally fills more orders on the winning side than the losing side, creating mechanical directional edge without directional intent
Kalshi continues to offer crypto price contracts (BTC/ETH above/below threshold markets) with regular expiry windows
Settlement fees remain in the 1-7 cent per contract range and do not increase to levels that eliminate spread-capture profitability
Binance/Coinbase WebSocket feeds remain available for real-time reference price tracking to anchor Bayesian probability estimates

The six non-predictive structural edges (base rate neglect, cross-market inconsistency, mechanical price moves, cross-platform comparison, certainty overpaying, time decay mispricing) remain exploitable on Kalshi due to persistent cognitive biases in crowd-sourced pricing
Order amendment (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend) preserves FIFO queue priority when price moves favorably for counterparty, enabling efficient ladder management without losing queue position

components.name: StoikovPricingEngine
components.description: Core quoting engine implementing the Stoikov-Avellaneda optimal market-making model. Computes reservation price and optimal spread based on inventory position, volatility, and time to contract expiry. Reservation price formula: r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t), where r=reservation price, s=mid price, q=inventory position, gamma=risk aversion parameter, sigma=volatility estimate, T=expiry time, t=current time. Optimal spread formula: delta = gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1 + gamma/kappa), where kappa is the market order arrival rate estimated from trailing fill frequency. The reservation price determines quote center; the optimal spread determines quote width. The spread floor must account for expected Kalshi settlement cost: effective_min_spread = max(min_spread, expected_settlement_fee * 2). The model naturally becomes more aggressive (wider quotes) when inventory is low and more defensive (tighter, skewed away from exposure) when inventory accumulates. Time-to-expiry component (T-t) causes spreads to widen as expiry approaches and inventory risk increases — critical for short-duration Kalshi contracts. All values in cents (Kalshi's native unit). Outputs bid and ask prices for both YES and NO sides.
responsibilities: Compute reservation price r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) using current inventory, volatility, and time to expiry
Compute optimal spread delta = gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1 + gamma/kappa) using estimated market order arrival rate
Apply settlement-fee-aware spread floor: effective_min_spread = max(min_spread, expected_settlement_fee * 2)
Output bid and ask prices for both YES and NO sides, ensuring YES_bid + NO_bid <= 100 - min_target_spread
Accept inventory state from InventoryManager (q parameter) and probability estimate from BayesianProbabilityUpdater

Recalibrate kappa (arrival rate) every 30 seconds from rolling fill count over trailing 60s — expected to be lower on Kalshi than higher-volume venues, which correctly widens optimal spread for thinner books
Enforce gamma tuning per market: 0.1 (conservative) to 0.5 (aggressive) — controls how aggressively quotes skew away from inventory

components.name: BayesianProbabilityUpdater
components.description: Maintains internal fair-value probability estimate for each contract using Bayesian updates anchored to external CEX reference prices. Ingests signals from Binance and Coinbase WebSocket feeds, order flow imbalance, and historical base rates. Updates before the market has fully repriced. Formula: P(H|D) = P(D|H) * P(H) / P(D). Prior P(H) initialized from CEX-derived probability (distance between spot and strike using short-term log-normal model). Kalshi orderbook mid-price used only as sanity check (flag if divergence > 10%) to avoid reflexive feedback loop from quoting on the same market used for the prior. Likelihood P(D|H) computed from CEX price movement magnitude and direction relative to contract strike. Posterior blended toward uniform prior via forgetting factor for rapid adaptation. Can integrate structural edge signals from StructuralEdgeDetector as additional Bayesian evidence to shift probability estimates when non-predictive mispricings are detected.
responsibilities: Maintain per-contract probability estimate using Bayesian update P(H|D) = P(D|H)*P(H)/P(D)
Initialize prior from CEX-derived probability (spot price vs strike distance via log-normal model)
Update on every CEX price tick or every 500ms, whichever is more frequent
Apply forgetting factor: posterior_adjusted = 0.95*posterior + 0.05*0.50 (half-life ~6.6s for rapid adaptation)
Flag divergence > 10% between internal estimate and Kalshi orderbook mid-price
Accept structural edge signals from StructuralEdgeDetector as additional evidence for probability revision
Compute minimum 3 percentage-point divergence threshold before adjusting quotes

components.name: BidLadderManager
components.description: Places and maintains laddered limit orders across multiple price levels on both YES and NO sides simultaneously via the Kalshi REST API. Deploys orders in 1-cent increments spanning a configurable range around the current mid-price. Manages order lifecycle: placement (POST /portfolio/orders), amendment (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend for price and/or quantity), batch creation (POST /portfolio/orders/batched for up to 20 orders), batch cancellation (DELETE /portfolio/orders/batched for up to 20 orders), quantity decrease (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/decrease), and fill tracking via WebSocket or polling GET /portfolio/fills. Uses order amendment instead of cancel-and-replace to preserve FIFO queue priority (queue position maintained when amending to a better price for counterparty). Uses batch operations to deploy/refresh entire ladders in a single API call. Monitors queue position via GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions to estimate fill probability and optimize ladder placement. Supports up to 200,000 max open orders. Ladder deployment speed is critical if Kalshi uses FIFO matching — first orders at each price level get priority fills.
responsibilities: Deploy 10-15 level deep bid ladders on both YES and NO sides with 1-cent spacing
Use batch creation (POST /portfolio/orders/batched, up to 20 per call) for efficient ladder deployment
Use order amendment (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend) to modify price/count in-place, preserving FIFO queue priority
Use batch cancellation (DELETE /portfolio/orders/batched, up to 20 per call) for efficient ladder refresh
Refresh ladders every 3 seconds or on significant mid-price movement (>1 cent), whichever comes first
Enforce spread feasibility constraint: YES_bid_max + NO_bid_max <= 100 - min_target_spread at all times
Monitor FIFO queue positions (GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions) to estimate fill probability per resting order
Feed queue position data to NonLinearCurveDistributor for capital allocation optimization
Receive volume allocation per level from NonLinearCurveDistributor and size caps from KellySizer

components.name: NonLinearCurveDistributor
components.description: Computes non-linear order size distribution across the bid ladder. Allocates more capital to price levels near the current mid (high fill probability) and exponentially less to distant levels (low fill probability, high adverse selection). This is the single most important differentiator identified across all source material: the Curve Alchemist bot outperformed flat-ladder Ladder Larry by 52% ($18,920 vs $12,450 in 24h) and Merge Phantom by 92% ($18,920 vs $9,830). The exact optimal curve shapes are proprietary and require live testing — cannot be backtested. Possible shapes include power-law, quadratic, exponential decay from mid, sigmoid, or custom piecewise functions. The curve must adapt to current volatility: flatter in low-vol (more fills needed), steeper in high-vol (protect against adverse selection). Queue position data from BidLadderManager informs capital reallocation — levels where the bot has strong queue priority deserve more capital.
responsibilities: Compute non-linear volume allocation across 10-15 ladder levels using power-law (default exponent 1.5) or adaptive curve
Allocate 15-20% of total ladder capital at the level closest to mid, tapering to 2-3% at most distant level
Adapt curve shape to current volatility regime: flatter in low-vol, steeper in high-vol
Incorporate queue position data: increase allocation at levels where bot has strong FIFO queue priority
Redistribute when mid-price moves >2 cents or on order fill
Maintain total ladder capital deployment at 60-80% of available capital
Support iterative curve calibration via parameterized exponent tuning based on live fill rate data
outputs: volume_allocation_per_level (array of contract counts per price level)

components.name: InventoryManager
components.description: Tracks net inventory position across YES and NO contracts using Kalshi's portfolio API (GET /portfolio/positions). Enforces hard limits on directional skew. When inventory exceeds thresholds, skews quotes to attract fills that reduce exposure (widening spread on overweight side, tightening on underweight side). Feeds inventory state into StoikovPricingEngine via the q parameter. Must respect Kalshi's per-market position limits — query GET /markets/{ticker} for position_limit field and enforce as ceiling on total contracts held per side. Position merging (YES+NO=$1 at settlement) is the primary inventory reduction mechanism — the SettlementRecyclingEngine handles the execution, but InventoryManager signals when inventory justifies a merge/exit.
responsibilities: Track per-market YES and NO positions via GET /portfolio/positions
Compute normalized inventory skew: (YES_position - NO_position) / total_capital
Apply soft warning threshold (0.15): begin skewing quotes to rebalance
Apply hard halt threshold (0.40): halt new order placement on overweight side entirely
Enforce Kalshi per-market position limits: reduce order sizes at 90% of limit, halt at limit
Feed inventory state (q parameter) to StoikovPricingEngine for reservation price adjustment
Signal SettlementRecyclingEngine when opposing positions should be exited or held to settlement
Target inventory skew reduction to below 0.10 within 60 seconds of breach via quote adjustment

components.name: SettlementRecyclingEngine
components.description: Manages capital recycling through Kalshi's settlement mechanics. Kalshi settles contracts at expiry — YES pays 100 cents if event occurs, NO pays 100 cents if not. Capital recycling works through two mechanisms: (1) Natural settlement at contract expiry: holding both YES and NO positions yields guaranteed combined value minus settlement fees. (2) Active exit via opposing limit orders: sell existing positions or buy opposing side to offset. The system tracks opposing positions and calculates when it is more capital-efficient to hold to settlement vs exit early. Settlement fees (1-7 cents per contract) reduce recycling efficiency compared to fee-free merging on other platforms. The Merge Phantom bot earned +$9,830 in 24h through capital recycling specialization — most merges intentionally take small losses to free capital for higher-EV new orders. Without recycling, capital locks in losing positions and the bot stalls. CRITICAL UNKNOWN: must determine in Phase 0 whether Kalshi supports any form of position merging/netting for early capital release, or if hold-to-settle is the only path.
responsibilities: Track all opposing YES+NO positions per market and compute potential settlement value
Calculate hold-to-settle economics: combined acquisition cost + settlement fees vs guaranteed 100-cent payout
Calculate early-exit economics: opposing limit order fill price vs settlement path cost
Execute optimal strategy: hold-to-settle when combined cost + fees < 102 cents, else exit early if available
Track all settlements via GET /portfolio/settlements and reconcile expected vs actual proceeds
Immediately redeploy settled/exited capital to active ladders — no blockchain confirmation delays
Monitor fee structure changes via GET /series/fee_changes and adapt thresholds accordingly

components.name: StructuralEdgeDetector
components.description: Implements six non-predictive structural edge detection categories that complement core spread capture without requiring outcome prediction. Uses Claude API for analysis where pattern recognition across historical data and cross-market comparisons is needed. These edges inform adaptive spread width and position sizing — when structural detection identifies mispricing, the bot adjusts parameters rather than taking directional bets. All six edges exploit persistent cognitive biases and structural inefficiencies rather than transient information advantages, making them durable over time.
responsibilities: Base rate neglect detection: compare market-implied probability against historical frequency of similar outcomes (bills stall, scandals fade, campaigns recover) — flag when narrative-driven pricing diverges from base rates
Cross-market inconsistency detection: identify related contracts that contradict each other (e.g., candidate weak in state polls but strong nationally)
Mechanical vs real price move classification: distinguish information-driven moves from thin-orderbook noise in low-liquidity Kalshi markets
Cross-platform comparison: compare same event priced on Kalshi vs other platforms for structural arbitrage signals
Certainty overpaying detection: identify when crowds systematically overpay for high-confidence outcomes — known calibration bias
Time decay mispricing detection: flag markets staying too expensive as calendar narrows remaining possibilities
Output spread adjustment signals: widen quotes when structural edge is favorable (deploy more capital), narrow when edges are absent
outputs: edge_signals per contract (array of detected edges with magnitude)

components.name: SpreadCaptureTracker
components.description: Monitors and records every spread capture event. A spread capture occurs when the bot buys YES at P_buy_yes and NO at P_buy_no where P_buy_yes + P_buy_no < 100 cents, locking in guaranteed gross profit of (100 - P_buy_yes - P_buy_no) cents per contract. Net profit subtracts settlement fees on both sides. Tracks realized spread per trade, cumulative spread PnL (gross and net of fees), and effective spread width over time.
responsibilities: Record every spread capture event with YES price, NO price, gross spread, and net spread after fees
Track rolling 1-hour and 24-hour cumulative spread capture metrics (gross and net)
Alert when average net realized spread drops below 1.0 cent (approaching unprofitable territory)
Maintain running total of settlement fees paid via GET /portfolio/settlements
Report settlement fees as percentage of gross spread PnL — alert if exceeding 60%
Compute minimum target spread: 3 cents gross, net must cover settlement fees on settling side(s)

components.name: KellySizer
components.description: Computes risk-budget cap for each ladder level using a Kelly-derived heuristic. Formula: f = (b*p - q) / b where b is expected spread payout net of settlement fees, p is estimated fill probability from BayesianProbabilityUpdater, and q = 1-p. Applied as upper bound on notional exposure per level, not as theoretically optimal directional wager. Uses fractional Kelly (0.25x full Kelly) for safety — reduces variance at cost of lower growth rate. Ensures no single position exceeds 8% of total portfolio. Additionally capped by Kalshi per-market position limits.
responsibilities: Compute Kelly fraction f = (bp - q) / b for each ladder level using current probability estimate and net spread edge
Apply quarter-Kelly (0.25x) for conservative sizing that survives variance
Enforce hard 8% max single position cap regardless of Kelly output
Require minimum 3-cent net spread edge (after settlement fees) before sizing any position
Recalculate on every Bayesian probability update (every 500ms)
Cap Kelly output at Kalshi market-specific position limit from GET /markets/{ticker}
Feed size caps to BidLadderManager for order placement

components.name: RiskController
components.description: Top-level risk management layer with kill switches and circuit breakers. Monitors portfolio-level drawdown, daily PnL, and per-market exposure. Automatically halts trading when thresholds are breached. Can trigger OrderGroupManager for fast-path kill switch. Queries Kalshi portfolio state via GET /portfolio/positions, GET /portfolio/fills, and GET /portfolio/balance (in cents).
responsibilities: Monitor daily loss limit: halt all trading at -20% of starting daily capital
Monitor peak-to-trough drawdown: full system shutdown at -40%, require manual restart
Enforce per-market max exposure: 15% of total capital in any single contract
Limit max concurrent markets to 4 simultaneous active ladders
Trigger OrderGroupManager as fast-path kill switch on threshold breach
Send Telegram alerts on every threshold breach and daily summary
Poll GET /portfolio/balance to track available cash (cents), total portfolio value, and pending settlements

components.name: MarketDataFeed
components.description: Aggregates real-time data from multiple sources. Binance and Coinbase WebSocket feeds provide reference crypto prices for Bayesian updates. Kalshi REST API and WebSocket provide order book state, fill notifications, and contract metadata. Computes real-time mid-price, realized volatility (60-second rolling), order flow imbalance, and book depth metrics. Batch orderbook polling (GET /markets/orderbooks for up to 100 tickers) enables efficient multi-market monitoring.
responsibilities: Ingest Binance WebSocket (btcusdt@trade, ethusdt@trade) with <50ms tick-to-state latency
Ingest Coinbase Advanced Trade WebSocket (BTC-USD, ETH-USD ticker channel) as secondary reference
Poll Kalshi orderbook via GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook or batch via GET /markets/orderbooks (up to 100 tickers)
Subscribe to Kalshi WebSocket (wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2) for real-time orderbook and fill events
Compute 60-second rolling realized volatility (standard deviation of log returns) for Stoikov sigma parameter
Compute order flow imbalance and book depth metrics for market quality assessment
Provide full depth data from Kalshi orderbook — adapt spread calculations for thinner-than-typical books

components.name: ContractWindowScheduler
components.description: Manages lifecycle of trading across multiple contract windows. Monitors upcoming Kalshi crypto price contracts via GET /events and GET /markets. Filters for crypto price threshold markets (BTC/ETH above/below X). Pre-computes initial ladder parameters and triggers prompt order placement when new contracts become available. Handles graceful wind-down as contracts approach expiry.
responsibilities: Discover crypto price contracts via GET /events?category=crypto and GET /markets?series_ticker=<crypto_series>
Poll GET /markets every 60 seconds for newly opened contracts
Pre-compute ladder parameters 5 seconds before placing orders on new contracts
Cancel all open orders 30 seconds before contract expiry to avoid settlement risk
Manage up to 4 overlapping concurrent contract windows
Filter contracts: sufficient open interest, time to expiry > 2 minutes, current spread > 3 cents

components.name: KalshiRequestSigner
components.description: Handles stateless per-request authentication with Kalshi API using RSA-PSS key-pair signing. Every outgoing HTTP request is signed by: (1) generating millisecond timestamp, (2) concatenating '{timestamp_ms}{HTTP_METHOD}{path_without_query_params}', (3) signing with RSA-PSS (SHA-256 hash, MGF1-SHA256, salt_length=DIGEST_LENGTH), (4) base64-encoding signature. Three headers: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE. No login endpoint, no tokens, no session state — entirely stateless per-request auth.
responsibilities: Load PEM private key from KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH at startup
Sign every outgoing request with RSA-PSS (SHA-256, MGF1-SHA256, salt_length=DIGEST_LENGTH)
Attach KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE headers
Support both demo (https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2) and production (https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2) endpoints
Validate signing at startup with test API call (GET /portfolio/balance) — fail fast if broken

components.name: OrderGroupManager
components.description: Manages Kalshi order groups for aggregate risk management of bid/ask ladders. Order groups allow assigning multiple orders to a group with a rolling 15-second contract fill limit shared across all orders. Separate groups for YES-side and NO-side ladders prevent runaway inventory from fill bursts. Groups can be triggered as a fast-path kill switch (cancel all + block new orders).
responsibilities: Create separate order groups for YES-side and NO-side ladders (POST /portfolio/order_groups/create)
Set per-group fill limits (e.g., max 50 contracts per 15-second window per side)
Trigger groups as kill switch when inventory skew exceeds soft_warning_threshold
Reset matched contracts counter to resume trading after trigger investigation
Integrate with RiskController for fast-path emergency halt — faster than individual order cancellation

components.name: RFQMonitor
components.description: Monitors Kalshi's Request for Quote (RFQ) system as an additional profit center. When other participants submit RFQs, the system responds with competitive quotes derived from StoikovPricingEngine. Provides additional flow beyond passive ladder orders. Maximum 100 open RFQs at any time. Enhancement priority — implement after core ladder strategy is validated.
responsibilities: Poll GET /communications/rfqs for incoming RFQs on actively market-made contracts
Respond with competitive quotes (POST /communications/quotes) using Stoikov pricing output
Apply same spread and sizing logic as ladder orders
Respect max 100 concurrent open RFQs

components.name: StatePersistenceLayer
components.description: Persists system state for fault recovery and graceful shutdown/restart. On shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), triggers all order groups for fast-path cancel, persists full state, and exits cleanly. On restart, loads latest snapshot, reconciles with live Kalshi positions, and flags discrepancies before resuming.
responsibilities: Persist open orders, inventory, running PnL, settlement fee totals, and settlement history after every fill event and every 10s heartbeat
Use SQLite for initial deployment given low write volume
On shutdown: trigger all order groups, batch-cancel remaining orders, persist final state snapshot
On startup: load latest snapshot, reconcile with live Kalshi positions (GET /portfolio/positions), flag discrepancies
Store curve calibration data (fill rates per exponent setting) for NonLinearCurveDistributor optimization

architecture.data_flow: KalshiRequestSigner signs every outgoing API request with RSA-PSS (stateless, no login/token step) -> MarketDataFeed ingests Binance/Coinbase WebSocket ticks and Kalshi orderbook state (REST polling + WebSocket) -> BayesianProbabilityUpdater computes internal fair-value probability from CEX reference price movement, optionally incorporating StructuralEdgeDetector signals (six non-predictive edges: base rate neglect, cross-market inconsistency, mechanical price moves, cross-platform comparison, certainty overpaying, time decay mispricing) -> StoikovPricingEngine uses Bayesian probability, current inventory (q from InventoryManager), volatility, settlement fee estimate, and kappa (arrival rate) to compute reservation price r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) and optimal spread delta = gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1+gamma/kappa), with spread floor accounting for settlement costs -> NonLinearCurveDistributor allocates capital across price levels using power-law or adaptive curve weighting (the primary differentiator, 52% outperformance vs flat ladders), informed by queue position data from BidLadderManager -> KellySizer caps individual level sizes via f = (bp-q)/b at quarter-Kelly with 8% hard cap and Kalshi position limits -> BidLadderManager deploys ladders via batch operations (up to 20 orders per call), amends existing orders in-place to preserve FIFO queue priority -> OrderGroupManager assigns ladder orders to groups with rolling 15-second fill limits -> Fill events update InventoryManager and SpreadCaptureTracker -> SettlementRecyclingEngine tracks opposing positions, determines hold-to-settle vs early-exit strategy factoring settlement fees (1-7 cents/contract) -> RiskController monitors portfolio metrics via GET /portfolio/positions and GET /portfolio/balance (cents), can halt pipeline or trigger order groups as kill switch -> ContractWindowScheduler orchestrates contract discovery and lifecycle -> RFQMonitor responds to incoming RFQs as additional flow source -> StatePersistenceLayer persists state for fault recovery.
integration_points: Kalshi REST API (https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2) — RSA-PSS signed requests (stateless). Market discovery (GET /events, GET /markets, GET /markets/{ticker}). Order management: create (POST /portfolio/orders, 200K max open), amend (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend), decrease (POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/decrease), batch create/cancel (up to 20 per call). Order groups: create, trigger, reset. Portfolio: positions, fills, balance (cents), queue positions. Orderbook: single ticker (depth 0=all), batch (up to 100 tickers). Market data: trades, candlesticks. Historical: candlesticks for parameter backtesting. Exchange: schedule, fee changes. RFQ: incoming RFQs and quote responses. Subaccounts: up to 32 for capital isolation
Kalshi WebSocket API (wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2) — real-time orderbook updates and fill notifications
Binance WebSocket API (wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/) — real-time BTC/ETH price ticks for Bayesian probability updates and volatility computation
Coinbase Advanced Trade WebSocket API (wss://advanced-trade-ws.coinbase.com/v1) — secondary reference price feed for cross-validation
Telegram Bot API — real-time alerts on risk threshold breaches, daily PnL summaries, settlement fee reports
Claude API (anthropic SDK) — structural edge detection: six non-predictive edge categories for spread/sizing adjustment signals and cross-market inconsistency analysis

phases.name: Kalshi Platform Discovery & Knowledge Gap Resolution

risks.description: Kalshi matching engine may use pro-rata instead of FIFO: if Kalshi uses pro-rata matching, the entire speed-based queue priority strategy becomes irrelevant and the architecture must shift to capital-based sizing. This is the most critical unknown. FIFO rewards latency; pro-rata rewards capital deployed at each price level. The NonLinearCurveDistributor and queue position tracking are designed for FIFO — pro-rata would require fundamentally different capital allocation logic.
risks.mitigation: Resolve in Phase 0 before any implementation investment. If pro-rata confirmed: redesign NonLinearCurveDistributor to optimize for capital weight at each level rather than queue position, remove queue position tracking, relax latency requirements from 200ms to 1s, increase minimum capital requirement. Document architecture pivot in decision record.

risks.description: No position merging on Kalshi — capital efficiency drops dramatically: if Kalshi does not support any form of position merging/netting before settlement, the Merge Phantom approach is invalid and capital recycling depends entirely on contract expiry timing or active exit via opposing limit orders. Capital could lock for hours in losing positions with no early release mechanism.
risks.mitigation: Resolve in Phase 0. If no merging: redesign SettlementRecyclingEngine to prioritize active exit (opposing limit orders) over hold-to-settle, increase minimum capital to cover locked-position periods, focus on shorter-duration contracts where expiry releases capital faster, reduce max_concurrent_markets to preserve capital for active ladders.

risks.description: Spread compression below profitability threshold: as more bots enter Kalshi crypto markets, spreads narrow. Combined with settlement fees (1-7 cents/contract), net spread can become unprofitable. However, Kalshi's thinner orderbooks maintain wider natural spreads longer than high-volume venues — a structural advantage.
risks.mitigation: Monitor effective net spread (gross minus settlement fees) in real-time. Alert when trailing 1h average net spread < 1.0 cent. Pause quoting on markets with insufficient spread. Track settlement fees as percentage of gross PnL — if >60%, investigate fee-optimizing strategies. Diversify across contract types and durations.

risks.description: Sudden market reversal causing inventory overload: a sharp, fast price move fills many ladder levels on one side while the opposing side gets no fills, creating heavy directional exposure. This is the primary source of realized losses for market makers.
risks.mitigation: Hard inventory skew limits (halt at 0.40). Stoikov pricing automatically widens overweight-side quotes. OrderGroupManager provides fast-path kill switch (15-second rolling fill limits). Exit via opposing limit orders or hold to settlement. Daily loss limit (-20%) prevents catastrophic accumulation.

risks.description: Latency disadvantage and queue competition: if Kalshi uses FIFO matching, faster bots get priority fills at each price level. Consistently slower placement degrades fill rates and profitability. If Kalshi uses pro-rata, this risk is mitigated but capital requirements increase instead.
risks.mitigation: Target <200ms order placement latency from US-east-1. Pre-compute ladder parameters before contract open. Use order amendment (preserves queue position) over cancel-and-replace. Monitor fill rate — if <30%, investigate latency. Kalshi's thinner books may mean less fierce queue competition.

risks.description: Kalshi fee structure changes eliminating spread profitability: if settlement fees increase beyond 7 cents or new per-trade fees are introduced, spread capture profitability could be destroyed. Since fees are on settlement, increases affect the entire holding period retroactively.
risks.mitigation: Parameterize settlement_fee_estimate so changes propagate immediately to spread calculations. Monitor GET /series/fee_changes. Maintain breakeven fee model — if actual fees approach breakeven, reduce positions or pause. Design system to operate across a range of fee assumptions.

risks.description: Non-linear curve optimization is empirical and cannot be backtested: the primary differentiator (52% outperformance of Curve Alchemist over flat ladders) depends on curve shapes that require live calibration. No closed-form solution exists. Suboptimal curve during calibration period means leaving significant edge on the table.
risks.mitigation: Start with power-law exponent 1.5 as baseline from source material. Implement A/B testing framework to compare curve shapes (power-law, quadratic, exponential, sigmoid) with small capital. Persist fill-rate-per-level data in StatePersistenceLayer for analysis. Allocate Phase 5 paper trading for systematic curve calibration before live deployment.

risks.description: Risk management bug allowing oversized positions: a bug in Kelly sizing or inventory management allowing >50% portfolio in a single position could cause catastrophic loss. More dangerous than a bad strategy.
risks.mitigation: Multiple independent size checks: KellySizer cap (8%), RiskController per-market cap (15%), InventoryManager hard halt (0.40 skew), Kalshi per-market position limits, OrderGroupManager rolling fill limits. All must agree before order placement. Extensive unit/integration testing. Paper-mode validation of edge cases.

risks.description: Kalshi platform changes or API breaking changes: as a regulated exchange, Kalshi may change contract mechanics, settlement rules, fee structure, API endpoints, or position limits. Regulatory changes are more likely to be announced in advance but still require rapid adaptation.
risks.mitigation: Monitor Kalshi announcements and API changelog. Check API version via GET /exchange/status. Build abstraction layer between strategy logic and platform API. Maintain paper-mode capability for re-validation after changes.

risks.description: RSA private key compromise or misconfiguration: Kalshi uses RSA-PSS per-request signing. Key compromise enables authenticated API calls by attacker. Key misconfiguration prevents all API calls.
risks.mitigation: Restricted key file permissions (chmod 600). Never commit to version control. Validate signing at startup with test call (GET /portfolio/balance) — fail fast. Rotate keys periodically. Separate keys for demo vs production. Use subaccounts (up to 32) to isolate market-making capital.

success_criteria: Monthly return on deployed capital: 2-5% net of all costs (settlement fees, infrastructure). Kalshi's settlement fee model (1-7 cents/contract) replaces per-trade fees — net return calculated after all settlement costs. Measured as trailing 30-day realized PnL / average deployed capital.
Inventory neutrality: net inventory skew (|YES - NO| / total_capital) stays below 0.15 for 95% of operating time. Measured as time-weighted average absolute inventory skew over trailing 24 hours.

Spread capture rate: average net realized spread >= 1.5 cents per completed trade cycle (buy YES + buy NO + settle or exit), after deducting settlement fees. Measured as total net spread PnL / total completed cycles over trailing 24h.
Fill rate: >= 40% of placed ladder orders result in fills before cancellation or expiry. Measured per contract window, averaged over trailing 24h.

Capital recycling efficiency: average capital turnover >= 2.5x per day (lower target than merge-based systems due to settlement-based recycling and fee drag). Measured as total settled/exited capital / average deployed capital over trailing 24h.
System uptime: >= 99% during active contract windows. Measured as minutes actively quoting / total minutes with available windows.
Maximum drawdown: never exceed -20% daily drawdown or -40% peak-to-trough drawdown. Continuous monitoring with automatic kill switch enforcement.
Order placement latency: P95 < 200ms from decision to Kalshi API acknowledgment. Latency histogram logged for every submission.
Settlement fee ratio: settlement fees < 50% of gross spread PnL (at least half of gross captured retained as net profit). Measured over trailing 7 days.

Non-linear curve outperformance: non-linear distribution must produce >= 30% higher net PnL than flat equal-size distribution in A/B testing during Phase 5 paper trading, confirming the Curve Alchemist vs Ladder Larry differential.

Structural edge signal accuracy: StructuralEdgeDetector signals (six categories) must correlate positively with subsequent spread capture profitability — contracts flagged with structural edges should produce higher net spread than unflagged contracts, measured over rolling 7-day windows.

Paper trading gate (all conditions required before live capital): (1) average net realized spread >= 1.0 cent/cycle after fees, (2) inventory skew < 0.15 for >= 90% of time, (3) no single-day loss > -10%, (4) capital recycling >= 2x/day, (5) settlement fee ratio < 60% of gross PnL. Minimum 7 days on Kalshi demo API with 200+ completed trades.
notes:
v3.0 upgrades from v2.1 by integrating knowledge overview findings (de188a4e) and restructuring to conform to design-spec schema.

Key changes in v3.0:

1. PHASE 0 ADDED — Kalshi Platform Discovery: The knowledge overview identified four critical unknowns that must be resolved before implementation: (a) FIFO vs pro-rata matching engine — determines entire competitive strategy axis, (b) maker/taker fee structure — whether maker rebates exist, (c) position merging equivalent — capital efficiency depends on this, (d) API rate limits and WebSocket capabilities. Phase 0 gates all subsequent phases with a go/no-go decision.

2. SIX NON-PREDICTIVE STRUCTURAL EDGES INTEGRATED: The StructuralEdgeDetector component implements all six edge categories from source tweet_2038903376453259756 (base rate neglect, cross-market inconsistency, mechanical price moves, cross-platform comparison, certainty overpaying, time decay mispricing) as a meta-layer feeding into BayesianProbabilityUpdater and spread/sizing decisions. These exploit persistent cognitive biases and are durable over time.

3. NON-LINEAR CURVE EMPHASIS ELEVATED: The NonLinearCurveDistributor is now explicitly identified as the single most important differentiator based on Curve Alchemist's 52% outperformance over flat ladders. Phase 5 includes dedicated curve calibration with A/B testing across power-law, quadratic, exponential, and sigmoid shapes. A new success criterion requires >= 30% outperformance vs flat distribution.

4. POSITION MERGING REFRAMED FOR KALSHI: The SettlementRecyclingEngine now explicitly addresses the Kalshi-specific capital recycling challenge — no on-demand position merging like blockchain venues. Two paths: (a) hold-to-settle at expiry (guaranteed combined value minus fees), (b) active exit via opposing limit orders. Phase 0 must determine if any merging/netting mechanism exists.

5. QUEUE PRIORITY/FIFO MECHANICS CONDITIONED ON DISCOVERY: All FIFO-dependent logic (queue position tracking, order amendment for priority preservation, latency targets) is now explicitly conditioned on Phase 0 confirmation of FIFO matching. Architecture pivot path documented for pro-rata matching.

6. STOIKOV FORMULA SPECIFICS PRESERVED AND ENRICHED: Both formulas fully documented — reservation price r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) and optimal spread delta = gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1+gamma/kappa). Kappa (arrival rate) calibration, gamma tuning per market, time-to-expiry spread widening behavior all specified.

7. KALSHI-NATIVE THROUGHOUT: All references to other prediction market platforms replaced with Kalshi equivalents. All prices in cents (Kalshi native). Authentication via RSA-PSS per-request signing (stateless). Settlement-fee-aware spread floors. Per-market position limits. Order groups for aggregate risk. Batch operations. Subaccounts for capital isolation. Demo/production API switching.

8. PHASE STRUCTURE: 7 phases (0-6) with Phase 0 as critical discovery gate. Phase 5 dedicated to non-linear curve calibration and paper validation. Phase 6 covers live deployment with gradual scaling.

Remaining open questions: (1) Can RL automate non-linear curve optimization vs manual live-testing iteration? (2) What is the game-theoretic equilibrium for multiple market-making bots on the same Kalshi contract? (3) How do strategies perform during Kalshi-specific edge cases (low-volume, settlement windows, regulatory events)? (4) Can the six structural edges be integrated directly into Stoikov probability estimates as a unified system rather than separate modules?
